text: Casey's scope from Lesson 1 is explicit: AWS exists only to hold a copy of the app's data. Driftwood opens a new AWS account dedicated to exactly that, and Theo creates an S3 bucket, driftwood-app-backups, in us-east-1 for nightly database backups.

Versioning protects against a bad overwrite, and a lifecycle rule ages backups into Glacier after 30 days and expires them after a year, so a year of nightly backups doesn't become a permanent, growing cost.
Lesson 7's replication job needs its own narrow IAM role, with a policy allowing only s3 PutObject and ListBucket on this one bucket -- not a broad user with standing credentials.

The actual plan was two more steps before go-live: a bucket policy restricting access to just that replication role, and explicitly enabling S3 Block Public Access as a second, independent layer. Both are standard hardening for exactly this kind of bucket.

But between the IAM role here, wiring up replication in Lesson 7, and everything else from Lessons 4 and 5 still settling, that policy step gets pushed to right before launch -- and once launch becomes about the app, it never gets picked back up. Nothing looks obviously wrong today.
